name: Component contribution supported by selective perturbation and restoration
description: Support the component-specific contribution to a measured system output with selective perturbation, restoration and the actual construct, abundance, localization and bypass controls.

support.proposition: A specified molecular/cellular output changes with a defined component or interaction, and the available perturbation/restoration controls support that component-specific contribution within the tested system.

operands.instruction: Record actual genotype/construct and host, expression/preparation, partners, readout, condition and restoration/bypass comparison. Preserve independently measured abundance/stability/localization when present; an unmeasured control remains unknown. Use separate hypotheses for participation, activation, assembly and direct catalysis. Rescue can strengthen the restored relationship while does_not_discriminate the normal route; overexpression or nutrient bypass can be an alternative mechanism. observed_extent applies only to actual measured input/source geometry, clipped to original material; target_footprint can restrict that measurement. direct applies only when actual source subjects and the target proposition/conditions match. For another source subject use non-direct applicability. inferred_extent requires an explicit target_footprint bounded by the actual assigned original-input scope; missing target_footprint supplies no invented extent. context_allocation requires explicit context_account_scope and nonempty context_scope on both assessment and compatible account; it cannot carry target_footprint, creates no molecular measurement and is not a sequence map. Source residue numbers never become target coordinates. This measured-extent operand is for actual matching scoped source material only; direct never pairs with inferred_extent. Source facts from another protein/organism instead use the attributed operand.

qualifications: A deletion or active-site change is not automatically an interaction-only or catalysis-only perturbation. TsaE organisms/assay endpoints differ and remain unreconciled. Contact geometry is neither energetic necessity nor an independent functional assay. A silent single deletion retains overlap and condition-demand alternatives.

Retain actual source_ref, source_subject_refs, condition_refs and assumption_refs. The published examples below are instruction provenance about their named subjects; they are not observations of ybhP/b0790 and were not repeated to prepare this draft.

At construction and in decision context, resolve these observation kinds through annotation_support_routes for the actual caller-bound annotation policy; an entry does not supply universal component labels, select a projector, mask another kind, change a weight, or create a target finding. An unavailable route declaration remains unavailable.

Use actual retained assessments in a compatible annotation account. Selecting this entry earns nothing. The current caller-owned applicability × relation × extent arithmetic, same-component maximum, coherent-account integration and derived discrimination remain unchanged for this review basis. A finding qualification is not an automatic numeric discount; no independence, confidence or new score dimension is implied.
support.boundary: Existing references retain constructs and controls but do not prove causal entailment. This entry adopts no required control checklist, causal threshold or scientific acceptance gate. System attribution and isolated chemistry can remain merged numerically under the actual caller policy; that unresolved combination is not repaired by renaming the route.

evidence.observation: H. volcanii PilA1/3/4/5/6 showed PibD-dependent mobility shifts; PilA2 had no clear shift. Deleting all six abolished adhesion; individual plasmid-expressed pilins restored varying adhesion and, with archaellins also deleted, visible filaments. PilA1 carrying the FlgA1 mature hydrophobic domain remained expressed and PibD-dependent for processing but produced neither pili nor adhesion.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant Methods/Results and stated observations/captions; no independent filament composition measurement, image analysis, expression quantitation or complete FlaFind rerun. | Source observation limit: Native-only PilA2 did not support adhesion although plasmid expression did. Other pilins remained possible filament components, so pure homopolymers were not proven. The PilA3 hybrid was not expressed and is not an interpretable assembly-negative control. The −2 motif audit below is partial, not a full predictor test.

evidence.observation: Authors: ActS alone lacks detected PG cleavage; adding it activates amidases in vitro.
evidence.limit: Complete primary Results/Discussion/Experimental Procedures inspected. No raw fluorescence, chromatogram or microscopy reanalysis.

evidence.observation: Purified Cas1/Cas2 joins labelled protospacers covalently to plasmid DNA. Cas1 H208A and D221A are defective; Cas2 E9Q supports integration. Cas2 beta6-beta7 deletion fails to support the reaction. Cas1 alone gives low integration with Mn2+, and Cas2 substantially enhances integration.
evidence.limit: Three primary E. coli relevant Results/Methods inspected, with earlier other-species nuclease comparators explicitly limited; new descriptive deposited-coordinate comparison. No biological experiments or new annotation run. | Source observation limit: Cas2 is required for efficient tested complex behavior, not for every detectable Cas1 strand-transfer event under all conditions. These integration assays do not demonstrate every stage of immune protection or protospacer generation.

evidence.observation: E2: Authors: stable, septally localized variants fail normal cell separation and show impaired AmiB activation (Table 1).
evidence.limit: 2013 complete relevant Results/Discussion/Methods and Table1 read via primary BioC; 2010 primary abstract/targeted indexed results only. Actual PDBe molecule/contact/residue checks and Table1 parsing saved. No new structural alignment or binding assay.

evidence.observation: Authors: preformed partner complexes and controls support ternary assemblies; activity changes vary by hydrolase.
evidence.limit: Relevant full pull-down, affinity, ternary-complex, activity and synthase-association Results; scaffolding Discussion; corresponding MST/denaturation/complex/PG-digestion Methods inspected. Other proteomics/localization Methods not exhaustively read.

evidence.observation: T2: Authors 2019: switch variants retain robust ATPase yet lose efficient repeated t6A synthesis, separating hydrolysis from functional coupling.
evidence.limit: 2018 complete relevant single/multiple-turnover Results/Methods and Discussion; 2019 relevant full Results/Methods/Discussion; 2015 relevant binding/mutant Results, Discussion and full supplementary assay section inspected. No new time-course measurements or kinetic fits.

evidence.observation: dominant-negative ATPase perturbs cell size/division in an independent study.
evidence.limit: Both original full primary reports read at Results level; failed mutant interpretations in the PNAS study retained as a limit. Two papers count as one system case. | Group source-use limits: The original observation is a composite of two primary reports and two Sulfolobus species. evidence.observation: CetZ inactivation does not yield the FtsZ-like division defect. cetZ1 deletion prevents rods at motile halo edges; GTPase-mutant expression and envelope-associated dynamic structures reinforce shape participation.
evidence.limit: Full paper results and extended-data controls inspected; rod/motility relationship is condition dependent. | Group source-use limits: Deletion, dominant mutants and imaging share one study. A motility phenotype does not measure direct motor activity; the tested nonphenotype is not universal absence of division involvement.

evidence.observation: CRISPRi interactions identify envelope dependencies; bamB/dolP double deletion impairs growth and reduces BamA. DolP co-purifies with membrane-assembled BamA and redistributes from midcell under stress.
evidence.limit: Full Results, selected controls and published peer-review limitations inspected; no new phenotyping. | Group source-use limits: Co-purification is not direct binding or catalysis; genetics, purification and imaging are connected results in one study.

evidence.observation: Structure shows a periplasm-length hydrophobic tunnel. Lipid crosslinking places phosphate-bearing material inside it. Length and pore-loop mutants lose ability to complement a sensitized pqiAB/letAB detergent phenotype.
evidence.limit: Full primary Results on architecture, length threshold, pore-loop mutants and crosslinking read. No structural re-refinement. | Group source-use limits: Cryo-EM, crosslinking and complementation are different connected modalities; they are not three direct transport assays. Lipid identity, direction and net flux remain unresolved.

evidence.observation: Independent promoter tests separate minJ from swrA. Seven swarming suppressors hit minC/minD and repair other defects. MinD mislocalizes without MinJ; MinJ localization depends on DivIVA, with corresponding two-hybrid interactions.
evidence.limit: Full original publisher Results read, including promoter controls, suppressor selection and localization hierarchy. Later MinCDJ mechanism is not treated as already resolved by this 2008 study. | Group source-use limits: Seven selected suppressors are one screen, not seven independent support units. Two-hybrid/localization do not resolve every molecular mechanism or make the historical swarming label primary.

evidence.observation: Without PopZ, ParB-origin foci remain mobile; re-expression captures them at emerging polar PopZ. Co-IP includes ParB but not FtsZ. Filamented FtsZ-depleted controls retain polar origins, excluding filamentation alone.
evidence.limit: Two original full primary Results examined; shared discoveries grouped into one case, not counted as independent gene cases. | Group source-use limits: Two original Cell papers are grouped as one shared discovery. The composite original observation does not attribute each individual experiment to both papers; the selected first-source route is supported in the retained observation. Co-IP does not by itself establish every direct contact.

evidence.observation: UgtP amount and localization depend on nutrients/UDP-glucose pathway state. Mutants alter cell length. Purified UgtP inhibits FtsZ assembly, while localization changes are separable from gross protein abundance.
evidence.limit: Full Results on nutritional dependence, pathway controls and FtsZ assays inspected. | Group source-use limits: Cellular perturbations and purified FtsZ assays are connected study outputs, not independent proofs of every causal link. Native sensing remains bounded.

evidence.observation: dinR loss induces the neighboring yneA-yneB-ynzC operon. Deleting that operon suppresses filamentation; inducible YneA alone reinduces elongation, whereas YneB or YnzC do not. Operon deletion reduces mitomycin-C-induced elongation.
evidence.limit: Primary publisher full Results inspected, including whole-operon deletion, separate gene re-expression and negative YneB/YnzC controls. The newer 2026 FtsW mechanism paper remains an abstract-only unexamined follow-up; do not treat the 2003 FtsZ inference as current direct mechanism. | Group source-use limits: Connected 2003 controls do not establish direct FtsZ binding. The 2026 FtsW follow-up remains abstract-only and unexamined; it is not upgraded by the older primary-results coverage.

evidence.observation: Depletion specifically disrupts 16S 3-prime processing; other tested rRNA ends remain normal. 70S particles fall; deletion of rnr permits loss of yqfG.
evidence.limit: Full Results examined, including specificity controls and rescue. Same protein-family investigation group as cellular_ybeY; not independent replication of all E. coli claims. | Group source-use limits: Other tested ends being normal does not address every RNA substrate. The linked YbeY family case does not independently validate wholesale cross-species transfer.

evidence.observation: 2022: changing only the downstream CofD/FbiA partner changes the apparent precursor preference. Cognate mycobacterial pairs favor PEP, Mycetohabitans pairs 3-PG, tested archaeal pairs 2-PL. GPPG is trapped structurally.
evidence.limit: Relevant full primary results/discussion and assay/LC-MS/crystallography methods inspected in all three papers. No new flux measurements, crystallographic refinement or spectrum fitting.

evidence.limit: Relevant expression/reconstitution/assay methods, results, stoichiometry figures and discussion inspected; supplements not independently reanalyzed.

evidence.limit: Relevant purification, reconstitution, activity/complementation methods, cofactor results and EPR interpretation inspected; raw spectra not reprocessed.

evidence.limit: Full relevant primary body, methods and figure legends inspected; supplement synthesis/raw isotopologue data not independently reanalyzed.

evidence.limit: Relevant primary body and methods, including substrate tests, filtrate reconstitution and structure work, inspected.

evidence.observation: Many bioY loci associate with biotin biosynthesis/regulons, but only approximately one-third link to bioMN; some genomes lack obvious BioMN homologs. In heterologous E. coli, BioY alone transported biotin. Longer accumulation assays initially suggested BioMN dispensability; initial-rate substrate titrations showed the full system has greater affinity. BioM Walker-A mutation impaired efficient uptake.
evidence.limit: Comparative results, all transport/complex results, discussion, and assay/bioinformatics methods read from full paper. No membrane assay or phylogenetic reconstruction performed. | Group source-use limits: Heterologous uptake does not establish a native role across all BioY paralogs, so it is not assigned allele-linked native A109. Late accumulation and initial-rate readouts are related tests.

evidence.observation: Across MCR-containing archaeal genomes, MMP16 tracks sulfoacetaldehyde-biosynthesis genes and often clusters with them. Knockout growth in standard sulfide-containing medium showed a defect rather than absolute auxotrophy. Removing supplied sulfide uncovered CoM-dependent growth; complementation restored it. Methionine inhibition experiments implicated a possible L-ASST backup without proving its mechanism.
evidence.limit: Full genomic, growth, complementation, transcriptomic and cysteine-mutant results, discussion, and phylogenetic methods read. Author data/code not rerun; no purified-enzyme activity claimed. | Group source-use limits: No purified ComF activity or exact L-ASST backup mechanism is claimed. Comparative results and shared strains/media are connected evidence.

GcsR is a regulator, not a glycine-cleaving enzyme; direct ligand binding remains unknown.

evidence.observation: tcuC loss prevented tricarballylate but not citrate growth in Salmonella. tcuC alone enabled E. coli citrate growth; tcuABC was needed for tricarballylate growth. Point mutations and complementation/marker rescue implicated tcuRABC.

Recipient growth does not directly measure the proposed purified catalytic reactions.

evidence.observation: Wild type used pyrimidines for nitrogen at low temperature. Mutants/suppressors separated nitrogen release from toxicity control. RutG loss blocked uracil but not uridine use; in-vitro release of ammonium did not remove in-vivo requirements for RutC-E.

evidence.observation: Deletion of either nifI abolished rapid ammonium switch-off of acetylene reduction; complementation restored it. evidence.limit: Main complete switch-off/reversibility/physiology Results and culture/assay Methods; no direct protein-interaction work claimed from this paper. | Group source-use limits: Connected activity and physiological controls do not establish direct physical nitrogenase inhibition or make NifI a catalyst. Negative blot findings retain detection limits.

evidence.observation: LC-MS detected copper-yersiniabactin in infected mouse and patient samples. ybtS loss increased copper sensitivity; purified unoccupied yersiniabactin rescued, whereas copper-preloaded ligand did not. Catecholate removal changed copper toxicity in the opposite direction.

evidence.observation: A markerless C260V substitution removed excitation quenching in purified IsiA.
